title: The outbox: a queue of operations waiting for the network

videos.script:
In lesson 7 every row knew one thing: whether the server had it. {{row}} That is not enough. A session created, lengthened and deleted is three things the server needs to hear.

So the planner gets an outbox. {{outbox}} A table of operations, written in the same transaction as the change. Either both land, or neither does.

Then it drains. {{drain}} Oldest first, one at a time. When the network fails, it stops, and the next run starts from the same place.

Two refinements follow. {{compact}} Coalescing, which folds five operations into two without changing what the server ends up with. {{poison}} And the poison operation, the one the server will refuse every time. It moves aside, so the rest can pass, and it waits for the person to decide.
